title: 2017 AMC 8 Problem 12
statement: The smallest positive integer greater than \(1\) that leaves a remainder of \(1\) when divided by \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6\) lies between which of the following pairs of numbers?

solutions.text:
If a number leaves a remainder of \(1\) when divided by \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6,\) then it is one more than the least common multiple of these numbers. The least common multiple is \(60,\) so the smallest such positive integer is \(60 + 1 = 61.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Numbers with remainder \(1\) after division by \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6\) are one more than multiples of their least common multiple.
Find the least common multiple of \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6\), then add \(1\).
